questions.text: Which statement best explains how enzymes speed chemical reactions?
choices: They increase the free energy of the products
They convert endergonic reactions into spontaneous ones without any energy input
They add ATP directly to every substrate
They lower activation energy without being consumed in the reaction
questions.explain: Enzymes function as catalysts by lowering activation energy.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Catalysts do not change the overall free-energy difference between reactants and products.
Incorrect. Catalysts speed reactions but do not eliminate thermodynamic requirements.
Incorrect. Many enzymes do not use ATP at all.
Correct. Catalysts speed reactions by making it easier to reach the transition state.
questions.image_alt: Graph of reaction rate versus substrate concentration showing a rapid rise followed by a plateau at enzyme saturation.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of feedback inhibition in a metabolic pathway?
choices: It prevents unnecessary production of end products when enough product is already present
It ensures that product concentration always falls to zero
It permanently shuts down every enzyme in the cell
It makes each step require more ATP
questions.explain: Feedback inhibition is an efficient way to regulate pathways.
choice_explanations: Correct. End-product inhibition conserves resources and maintains homeostasis.
Incorrect. Feedback inhibition typically limits excess buildup rather than eliminating all product.
Incorrect. Feedback inhibition is pathway-specific and often reversible.
Incorrect. The advantage is regulation, not increased energy cost.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the electron transport chain in cellular respiration?
choices: To produce all ATP directly by substrate-level phosphorylation
To use electrons to build a proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis
To split glucose into two molecules of pyruvate
To fix carbon dioxide into sugars
questions.explain: The ETC creates the proton gradient used in chemiosmosis.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Most ATP from aerobic respiration comes indirectly through chemiosmosis.
Correct. Electron transport powers proton pumping, and the gradient powers ATP synthase.
Incorrect. That occurs during glycolysis.
Incorrect. Carbon fixation occurs in photosynthesis, not respiration.

questions.text: Why does reaction rate plateau at very high substrate concentration in many enzyme assays?
choices: The activation energy increases as substrate concentration rises
ATP is always required and has run out
The substrate no longer exists as a chemical
Most enzyme active sites are occupied, so enzyme availability becomes limiting
questions.explain: A plateau usually indicates enzyme saturation.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Catalyst and conditions determine activation energy, not substrate concentration alone.
Incorrect. Many enzyme reactions do not require ATP.
Incorrect. The substrate can still exist even when rate plateaus.
Correct. Once enzymes are saturated, adding more substrate has little effect.

questions.text: A reaction-rate graph rises quickly and then levels off as substrate concentration increases. Which conclusion is most strongly supported?
choices: Activation energy increased because more substrate was present
The substrate changes into a competitive inhibitor at high concentration
The enzyme becomes saturated at high substrate concentrations
The enzyme concentration increased during the assay
questions.explain: A saturation curve is classic evidence that enzyme availability is limiting at high substrate concentration.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. The plateau reflects saturation, not a higher activation energy.
Incorrect. Plateauing alone does not show substrate becomes an inhibitor.
Correct. The plateau indicates most active sites are occupied.
Incorrect. The graph does not imply more enzyme was added.

questions.text: An enzyme's activity peaks around 40°C and then drops sharply. What is the best explanation for the drop?
choices: The enzyme becomes a lipid above 40°C
Higher temperature always makes enzymes work faster forever
High temperature disrupts the enzyme's structure and active site
The enzyme permanently runs out of substrate at 40°C in every trial
questions.explain: The post-optimum decline is usually due to denaturation.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Macromolecules do not change class in this way.
Incorrect. Enzymes have optima and can denature at high temperature.
Correct. Loss of tertiary structure commonly reduces enzyme function above the optimum.
Incorrect. A temperature pattern alone does not imply all substrate vanished.

ATP is coupled to energy-requiring transport processes but not to passive diffusion
ATP is only used in photosynthesis
Passive diffusion requires more ATP than active transport
questions.explain: The experiment distinguishes ATP-dependent from passive processes.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Transport typically requires membrane proteins for specific movement.
Correct. Active transport needs energy, whereas passive diffusion does not.
Incorrect. ATP is used broadly across cell biology.
Incorrect. This reverses their energy relationships.
questions.image_alt: Cycle diagram showing ATP hydrolysis releasing energy and ADP plus phosphate being recharged using energy from cellular respiration or photosynthesis.
